dialogues.speaker: Euphrosiniya
dialogues.text: My house takes its name from Grand Duke Brahe Prokhorovitch Trubetskoy, Governor of Nod-Krai five hundred years ago.

dialogues.speaker: Euphrosiniya
dialogues.text: His title came to him through his adoptive father, a fae who gave his life in glorious service to His Majesty the Belyi Tsar. Even under the laws of that time, there was nothing improper about a human inheriting a fae's title.

dialogues.speaker: Euphrosiniya
dialogues.text: When Solovei the Torchforger asked the Tsaritsa to grant the borderlands autonomy, Grand Duke Brahe also appeared before the throne. There, he willingly gave up any claim to the land and all it held.

dialogues.speaker: Euphrosiniya
dialogues.text: He then entrusted the governor's palace to the Lightkeepers, who turned it into a military fortress. And that is how the Nod-Krai we know today came to be.

dialogues.speaker: Euphrosiniya
dialogues.text: Tch... I would very much like to know which ungrateful bard in the borderlands first made up those rumors about my ancestor...

dialogues.speaker: Euphrosiniya
dialogues.text: They claim — and please, you must not believe this — that he was made a fool of by Reed Miller's companion, and that he greedily sought some so-called "Great Treasure."

dialogues.speaker: Euphrosiniya
dialogues.text: Those lying, good-for-nothing fools are no better than the nobles on the Veche. If I ever learn who started that tale...
